places.name: Albert and Bessie Kronkosky State Natural Area
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Boerne (nearest city)
Bandera (county seat)
places.blurb: Hill Country ranch the Kronkoskys willed to Texas: golden-cheeked warbler habitat, springs and a view of the stars. Not open yet.
places.status_note: Not open. Under construction; TPWD has not set an opening date. Camping is planned for later, not offered now.
places.notes: TEN CANDIDATES for my name, chosen at the end: Ephemeris (chosen), Gazetteer, Benchmark, Trigpoint, Nadir, Lodestar, Culmen, Dusklight, Plumbline, Meridian. Wikipedia says the opening is planned for late fall 2026; that is not on the TPWD page, so I did not use it. Acreage: TPWD says 3,794 and Wikipedia says 3,814; TPWD used. County: Wikipedia lists Bandera and Kendall, and the park spans both; I did not check the point against the county line. TPWD point is 0.0 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Caddo Lake State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Marshall (Starr Family Home State Historic Site)
Karnack (Lady Bird Johnson's childhood home)
Jefferson (once Texas's largest inland port)
places.blurb: Bald cypress and Spanish moss on Big Cypress Bayou, with 1930s CCC cabins, a dining hall and paddling on Saw Mill Pond.
places.notes: 46 campsites run from water-only to full hookup, plus screened shelters, cabins and group sites (TPWD). Tent use is inferred from the water-only sites; the page does not use the word tent. Acreage 484 is Wikipedia's figure (citing the TPWD Official Guide p.114). The 26,810-acre number on the TPWD page is Caddo Lake itself, not the park. TPWD page says Harrison County is under an emerald ash borer firewood quarantine: buy firewood locally. TPWD point is 1.2 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Dinosaur Valley State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Glen Rose (nearest town, the Dinosaur Capital of Texas)
Somervell County Museum (Glen Rose)
places.blurb: Dinosaur tracks in the Paluxy riverbed, 20 miles of trails, a river to swim, fish and paddle, and a horse-friendly South Primitive Area.
places.status_note: Trails and track visibility can close in wet weather; the TPWD page asks visitors to check before arriving.
places.notes: The TPWD page names campsites and group sites but does not split campsites into tent or RV, so camping_kinds lists only group. Acreage 1,524.72 is Wikipedia's figure. Wikipedia, citing 2025-2026 news, describes a proposed power-line and data-center project near the park that is contested; that is second-hand, not checked against primary sources, and not used in any field. TPWD point is 0.9 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Goliad State Park and Historic Site
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Goliad town square and 1894 courthouse (TPWD page)
Zaragoza Birthplace State Historic Site (outlying unit per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: San Antonio River campsites beside a reconstructed mission on the southern edge of Goliad, with screened shelters and a group hall.
places.notes: Campsites run from water-only to full hookup and there are five screened shelters (TPWD). Tent use is inferred from the water-only sites. Acreage 276 is Wikipedia's whole-park figure from its lead; its infobox gives 188.3 for the main unit. TPWD point is 0.0 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Lake Brownwood State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Brownwood (nearest city)
Lake Brownwood (the 7,300-acre reservoir the park sits on, TPWD)
places.blurb: CCC-built cabins, lodges and a stone hall on the shore of Lake Brownwood, with water-only tent sites, full hookups and screened shelters.
places.notes: TPWD lists water-only tent sites, sites with water and electric, 20 full hookup sites, 10 screened shelters, two- and four-person cabins and lodges for four to 26. Acreage 1,406.5 is from Wikipedia. Wikipedia says the state acquired 869 more acres in 2023 (second-hand); it is unclear whether 1,406.5 includes them. TPWD point is 0.0 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Lyndon B. Johnson State Park and Historic Site
places.coord_point: park headquarters (TPWD page prints the HQ address directly above the coordinate)
nearby: LBJ Ranch (adjacent, per TPWD page)
Fredericksburg (German architecture and the National Museum of the Pacific War, per TPWD page)
places.blurb: Pedernales River park honoring LBJ: a living history farm, 1860s and 1870s log cabins, a pool in summer and a river for fishing.
places.status_note: The farm is closed the last Tuesday of each month and on Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day; trails and day-use areas are open until dark (TPWD).
places.notes: The TPWD page mentions only a small camping area that youth groups can reserve; no general campsites are listed, so camping_kinds is group only. Acreage 732.75 is from Wikipedia; the TPWD page does not print it. TPWD point (HQ) is 0.0 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Palo Pinto Mountains State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Strawn (nearest town)
Tucker Lake (90-acre lake inside the park; electric motors only, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Former ranch about 75 miles west of Dallas-Fort Worth: 16 miles of multiuse trails, a 90-acre lake, and walk-in tent and equestrian sites.
places.status_note: Open daily 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. (TPWD). Fills on weekends and holidays. Wikipedia dates the public opening to March 1, 2026 (second-hand).
places.notes: Acreage 4,871 is printed on the TPWD page. Wikipedia lists Palo Pinto and Stephens counties; I used Palo Pinto because the point is near Strawn, but I did not check the point against the county line. TPWD lists water-and-electric sites, walk-in tent sites, hike-in primitive sites, equestrian sites and a group site. TPWD point is 1.4 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: South Llano River State Park
places.coord_point: park coordinate as printed by TPWD (point type not stated)
nearby: Junction (about 5 miles, per DarkSky's 2017 release)
Interstate 10 (the park is just off I-10, per DarkSky's 2017 release)
places.blurb: Dark Sky Park on the South Llano River: tubing and paddling, 22 miles of trails, and one of Central Texas's largest winter turkey roosts.
places.status_note: Day-use area is open only 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. from Oct. 1 to March 31 to protect the turkey roost (TPWD). Stargazing has a night activity fee.
places.notes: Dark Sky designation is from DarkSky International's news item, published February 14, 2017. The darksky.org places list is JavaScript-rendered and only partly readable in this run, so the designation rests on that news item. Bortle 3 is from the 2017 release, not a current reading. The TPWD stargazing page returned 404, so there is no park reading. Campsites: most have water and electric, six walk-in sites have water (tent use inferred), five primitive hike-in sites have a chemical toilet and no water (TPWD). TPWD point is 0.6 km from the Wikipedia point; TPWD used.

places.name: Lake Meredith National Recreation Area
places.coord_point: recreation area's general point from Wikipedia infobox; NOT the headquarters (the NPS pages print the HQ address, not coordinates)
places.county: Hutchinson (the NRA also spans Moore and Potter, per Wikipedia)
nearby: Borger (hotels and restaurants, per NPS directions)
Amarillo (about 30 miles south of the lake, per Wikipedia)
Alibates Flint Quarries (NPS unit linked from the NPS home page)
places.blurb: Panhandle reservoir below 200-foot canyons: free first-come shore camping, RV hookups at Sanford-Yake and the Fritch Fortress overlook.
places.notes: Coordinates are Wikipedia's infobox point, not the HQ. NPS directions page: headquarters at 419 E. Broadway, Fritch. NPS camping page: 10 fee RV sites at Sanford-Yake with electric and water hookups, reserved by calling 806-865-3131; other sites are free and first-come; Fritch Fortress takes RVs with no hookups; Cedar Canyon is beach camping with no individual sites. NPS allows camping anywhere in the NRA for up to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period, 60 days a year, with fires only in grills and fire rings (basis for dispersed). Acreage 44,978 is NPS's figure. Wikipedia's coordinate is not verified against any NPS map.

places.name: Lyndon B. Johnson National Grassland
places.coord_point: grassland point from GNIS via Wikipedia; NOT the Decatur district office (the Forest Service page gives the office address but no coordinates)
places.county: Wise (the grassland also reaches Montague, per Wikipedia)
nearby: Decatur (nearest town; district office at 1400 US Highway 81/287)
Clear Lake (Unit 41 of the LBJ grassland, USFS page)
TADRA Point Trailhead (LBJ Multi-Use Trail, about 75 miles, USFS page)
places.blurb: Grassland camping near Decatur (some areas charge a small fee), with about 75 miles of LBJ Multi-Use Trail for hikers, bikers and riders.
places.notes: Office: Caddo/Lyndon B. Johnson National Grasslands, 1400 US HWY 81/287, Decatur TX 76234, (940) 627-5475 (USFS offices page). The USFS recreation page covers the Caddo and LBJ grasslands together. Official listings show four campgrounds and two horse camps; Black Creek has 14 walk-in sites and Bois D'Arc has 26 campsites, neither split by tent or RV, so camping_kinds lists only equestrian. Wikipedia says camping is mostly free, allowed in virtually any area, with a few marked fee areas (second-hand); the USFS page does not say that, so dispersed is not listed. Acreage 20,309 is Wikipedia's figure from a 2013 USFS land-area table, so it is dated. The point is Wikipedia's GNIS coordinate, about the middle of the grassland.
